chapter: Hard times and working bands of the 1930s
title: Whitewashing tombs in the St. Louis cemeteries and the hard times of c. 1929
summary: Rene worked whitewashing tombs in St. Louis cemeteries, paying permits to the priest.

story.theme_name: Making a living: hard times, day jobs and scarce work
story.community_name: The Depression years and the WPA band

blocks.x: Yeah, I worked in St. Louis graveyard.
We were in there too, working in St. Louis graveyard.
We used to whitewash tubes. Yeah, we used to whitewash tubes. Didn't tell you that either. No. Some do, yeah. That much work? Wow. Yes, sir.
We? Working for the section? Yeah, we was working for the section, you see.
Then he got me a job in there hustling around, you see. Had to pay two and a half of permits, you see, to the priest.
You see, the priest owned them graveyards, you know.
St. Louis number one, number two, number three. And we working there. Things were a little kind of tight then, you know. When was this? I was in there.
When was this? That was in there.
Let's see, I think that was back up in the 28 or 29 or something like that. Where the back in there?
Things were rough, huh? Yeah, things were rough. The PWA, man.

We didn't play no games for a couple of people who was scared of playing for. You didn't know where you were going to get your money or not. We used to play just with wives. We know we got our money, you see. And the dancing used to be mostly on Friday, Saturday night, Thursday night, you know, Tuesday night.
